title: Multiple sclerosis disease-modifying drugs
ariaLabel: Schematic of multiple sclerosis: immune cells are activated, leave lymph nodes, cross the blood-brain barrier, and attack myelin. Interferon beta and glatiramer shift the immune balance, fingolimod traps lymphocytes in lymph nodes, natalizumab blocks entry across the blood-brain barrier, and anti-CD20 antibodies deplete B cells.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Immune activation
nodes.info: Autoreactive T and B cells become active outside the brain.

nodes.label: Lymph node exit
nodes.info: Lymphocytes leave lymph nodes along a sphingosine-1-phosphate gradient.

nodes.label: Lymphocytes in blood
nodes.info: Circulating lymphocytes that can reach the brain.

nodes.label: Brain entry
nodes.info: Lymphocytes stick to and cross the blood-brain barrier using alpha-4 integrin.

nodes.label: Cells in the brain
nodes.info: Immune cells that have entered the brain.

nodes.label: B cells
nodes.info: B cells that carry CD20 take part in the immune attack.

nodes.label: B cell effect
nodes.info: B cell activity in the disease.

nodes.label: Relapse activity
nodes.info: A teaching score for new immune attack on the brain's myelin. It does not show reversal of existing disability.

edges.label: immune balance
edges.info: Interferon beta and glatiramer acetate shift the immune balance towards anti-inflammatory activity and lower new relapses modestly. Interferon beta causes flu-like symptoms.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: lymphocyte exit
edges.info: Fingolimod and similar drugs act on S1P receptors so lymphocytes are trapped in lymph nodes and fewer reach the brain. They can slow the heart at the first dose.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: integrin adhesion
edges.info: Natalizumab blocks alpha-4 integrin so fewer cells enter the brain. It carries a risk of progressive multifocal leucoencephalopathy (JC virus).
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: B cell depletion
edges.info: Ocrelizumab, ofatumumab and rituximab remove CD20 B cells. They raise infection risk and can lower antibody levels.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Interferon beta and glatiramer shift immune balance, fingolimod traps lymphocytes in lymph nodes, natalizumab blocks entry to the brain, and anti-CD20 antibodies remove B cells. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Steroids for relapses, cladribine, teriflunomide, dimethyl fumarate, progressive disease, symptomatic treatment, pregnancy planning, PML and infection monitoring, MRI follow-up and cost are left out. Relapse activity is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
